title: European summer precipitation
abstract: Abstract. Observations indicate that parts of Europe have experienced summer drying over recent decades. There is, however, substantial uncertainty in terms of precipitation changes projected by global climate models, underscoring the need for improved understanding to guide adaptation. Here, we analyse changes in European summer precipitation with global warming in 35 CMIP6 Earth system Models using a regional atmospheric energy budget framework. Over the historical period we compare these models to two reanalysis datasets, ERA5 and MERRA-2, as well as the E-OBS daily gridded observational dataset. Although ERA5 and MERRA-2 compare well to observed precipitation, they diverge substantially from each other and exhibit large discrepancies with the CMIP6 models when evaluating other terms in the atmospheric energy budget. In future projections, variability across models increases relative to the historical period for the changes in precipitation, sensible heat and the dry static energy flux divergence, highlighting the uncertainties in the magnitude of these terms. Nevertheless, the models show consistent agreement on the projection of summer drying over continental Europe with anthropogenic forcing over time.
problem: Global climate models exhibit substantial uncertainty in projecting European summer precipitation changes, a challenge stemming from large model-to-model discrepancies in representing key components of the atmospheric energy budget, which complicates adaptation planning.
method: This study analyzes changes in European summer precipitation using a regional atmospheric energy budget framework, comparing 35 CMIP6 models against reanalysis and observational datasets for historical and future periods to investigate projected summer drying and its underlying uncertainties.
task: The task is to analyze changes in European summer precipitation with global warming using a regional atmospheric energy budget framework, comparing 35 CMIP6 models to reanalysis and observational datasets to understand uncertainties in historical and future projections of summer drying.
innovation: This paper uses a regional atmospheric energy budget to analyze European summer precipitation in 35 CMIP6 models, revealing large discrepancies with reanalysis datasets and attributing the spread in future drying projections to uncertainties in the dry static energy flux divergence term.

The Mediterranean region has especially experienced a drying since the 1980s and is characterized as a climate hotspot, due to the anticipated continuation of warming and drying (Lionello and Scarascia, 2018).
There has also been an increase in summer droughts over continental Europe since 1901, except over Northern Europe (Hänsel et al., 2022).

Reanalysis data from ERA5 (Hersbach et al., 2020) and MERRA-2 (Gelaro et al., 2017) are compared with the CMIP6 models. ERA5 has a resolution of 0.25° for latitude and longitude, while MERRA-2 has a coarser resolution of 0.5° in latitude and 0.625 in the longitude.

The dry static energy flux divergence is calculated using data at 3h temporal resolution, interpolated from terrain-following coordinates to pressure levels and then integrated in the vertical.

To further study the spread in the models and how they compare to the reanalysis and observational data over Europe, the fluxes are spatially averaged over land in the European region as well as in the three additional regions (see Fig. 3b and methods). These additional regions include a Mediterranean region where Fig. 1 indicates a general drying, a Central European region where the change from drying to wetter conditions is likely to be located, and a Northern European region which is expected to get wetter.

The change in future projections of precipitation is a drying over continental Europe and an increase over Northern Scandinavia, with a decreasing area where models disagree with higher forcing (no statistically significant change in precipitation).

Similar to older versions of GCMS, MERRA-2 has a too transparent atmosphere causing too little SW radiation to be absorbed in the atmosphere compared to observations, while ERA5 overestimates the absorption (Wild and Bosilovich, 2024).

Even though the signal in the precipitation change since 1980 is not strong in the CMIP6 models, future projections show a summer drying over Mediterranean and Central Europe, as well as more precipitation over Northen Scandinavia.
